title: Compact checkpointing and reclaimed delivery for interrupted token streams
creator: Ava Nguyen
description:
Problem: When clients disconnect or time out mid-generation we currently retain full in-memory generation state (large KV cache + buffered deltas) for the session TTL, which raises memory pressure and makes backpressure/eviction decisions brittle. Additionally, clients that reconnect either must restart generation or rely on heavyweight resume semantics that are expensive to store and transfer.

Goal: Introduce a compact checkpointing scheme and a reclaimed-delivery policy to reduce footprint for interrupted token deliveries while preserving a high chance of client resume and preventing resource amplification under backpressure. The design aims to balance memory/disk footprint, resume success rate, and complexity of compatibility with existing streaming and tool-calling flows.

Proposed design summary:
- Compact checkpoints: periodically emit a minimal checkpoint object for active streaming sessions containing: sequence offset, condensed KV-cache fingerprint (delta bloom + small checksum), and a compact op-log of last N token spans (byte-prefixed). Checkpoints are designed to be O(1-10KB) instead of full cache snapshots.
- Two-tier retention: keep recent full in-memory session state for active connections and short-lived checkpoints for recently disconnected clients. Older checkpoints are offloaded to low-cost storage with strict TTL and a smaller index.
- Reclaimed delivery policy: if a reconnect occurs within checkpoint TTL, attempt a lightweight reconciliation: verify checkpoint fingerprint against current model cache; if compatible, continue from checkpoint with a minimal KV rehydration protocol (pull only missing KV ranges). If mismatch, fall back to deterministic restart and surface a structured event to the caller.
- Backpressure coupling: checkpoints are emitted when the local batch queue drains below a threshold or at token-count intervals; this reduces checkpoint churn under sustained high-throughput. When system-wide memory pressure is detected (adaptive eviction), we accelerate checkpoint offload and trim kept in-memory generations to 0 or 1 per user depending on SLO tier.
- Accounting & SLOs: record resume_success_rate, checkpoint_emit_latency, average checkpoint size, reclaimed_bytes, and cost delta per resume. Create dashboard on Console with per-route metrics and alerting for resume_rate drops.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Checkpoint frequency vs resume probability: more checkpoints increase resume chances but raise I/O. We'll validate with 3 candidate frequencies (every 50, 200, 1000 tokens).
- Fingerprint collision risk: condensed fingerprints must be tuned to minimize false-positive compatibility checks.
- Tool/function-calling interactions: for streaming tool calls that mutate external state, checkpoints will include tool-call idempotency metadata; reconnect logic must not replay side-effects.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation stores compact checkpoints with median size < 8KB under standard workloads (chat-like prompts).
- Resume success rate >= 85% for reconnects within 60s in canary tests for the P1 workload.
- Under synthetic disconnection storm (1000 concurrent clients disconnecting), memory pressure prevents OOM and reclaimed bytes measured meet target (>25% memory reduction).
- Console dashboards added and alerts for resume_success_rate < 75%

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design checkpoint wire format and small proto (storage-friendly).
2) Implement in runtime: periodic emitter, checkpoint store interface, rehydration handshake.
3) Add adaptive eviction hook and integrate with autoscaler signals for Dedicated.
4) Add structured events for API consumers and update SDK docs.
5) Canary rollout and metric validation.

References:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/INF/compact-checkpointing-design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2481
comments: 2026-01-14 - Initial triage: PMs agree this addresses a common escape path for disconnected sessions. Marked P1 for Q1 risk-reduction.

2026-01-25 - Design review notes: Add explicit idempotency tokens for tool calls; Diego to prototype fingerprint algorithm options (bloom vs rolling-hash). Action: Diego to deliver microbenchmarks by 2026-02-05.
2026-02-06 - Microbenchmarks uploaded: bloom-filter (1.2KB) + 64-bit rolling-checksum gives low collision on our corpora. Chosen default: 128-bit rolling hash + 512-byte bloom for most routes.
2026-02-12 - Implementation update: checkpoint emitter added to runtime loop; initial store uses local fast-path + S3 offload for long-tail. Needs QA on race between eviction and rehydration.

2026-02-22 - QA notes: deterministic restart fallback works. Two issues found: (1) tool-call idempotency header not persisted in checkpoint for function-calls; (2) checkpoint TTL cleanup job misses stale index entries. Created follow-ups ENG-131245 and ENG-131246.
2026-02-28 - Code review: Runtime PR approved with minor nits. Preparing canary on dedicated-qa cluster. Metric dashboards added to console-ops dashboard group.
